speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: A vital part of any country's water supply management is ensuring water quality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Singaporeans enjoy the convenience of clean and wholesome water at the turn of a tap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This does not come easy, but is achieved through forward planning and careful implementation of sound policies and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The Bill before the House today seeks to ensure that the quality of the water supplied to Singaporeans remains uncompromised, even with changing conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Plumbing is essential for our access to potable water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While the Public Utilities Board (PUB) ensures the safety and adequacy of the water it produces, owners of premises are responsible for the maintenance of their building's internal pipes and water tanks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Plumbing is also important for the protection of public health, as a well-functioning sanitary system channels used water away effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Currently, PUB regulates water service plumbers who carry out works on the potable water system, but not sanitary plumbers who carry out works on sanitary appliances and facilities, as the latter were deemed less complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While this regime has not caused issues thus far, our water and sanitary plumbing systems are becoming more integrated and complex, particularly in large-scale and high-rise buildings, with concealed piping systems becoming more common.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: There is also increasing adoption of alternative water systems in commercial and industrial developments like NEWater and rainwater harvesting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: All these systems must be built properly by competent plumbers to prevent cross-contamination between the potable water system and the non-potable or sanitary systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While we have not experienced cases of cross-contamination, this has happened elsewhere, such as in Alameda City, California, where a cross-connection between the city’s drinking water supply and a non-potable irrigation well rendered parts of the city’s water supply undrinkable for days.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will, therefore, strengthen the regulation of critical plumbing works and ensure that plumbers have the skills and knowledge to undertake complex works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For instance, sanitary pipes need to be laid such that they are both air-tight and water-tight, otherwise public health may be affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB will specify eligibility requirements, such as training and competency requirements, for all LPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Home owners, consumers and developers will be assured of the quality of work carried out by these trained and licensed plumbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The Bill will also provide for PUB to give directions to LPs as well as professional engineers to rectify works which contravene requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: During the transitional period, eligible incumbent plumbers can continue to carry out their respective vocations pending receipt of the new LP licences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Since the announcement of the proposed LP scheme in April last year, PUB has been working closely with the industry to facilitate the entry of plumbers into the LP scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The remaining plumbers are either undergoing the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) Academy's Builder Certificate Plumbing and Pipefitting Course and/or PUB's two- or three-day conversion course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: They will qualify as licensed plumbers after passing the requisite assessments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Other than helping existing plumbers upgrade their skills, we also want to encourage new entrants to join the profession.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Since the announcement of the scheme, 25 persons of varying backgrounds, ranging from those with GCE "O" level qualification to degree holders, have successfully completed the requisite courses by BCA Academy and PUB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Among them is 55-year-old Mr Lim Choon Sin, currently a mechanical and electrical contractor with GCE "O" level qualifications, and 36-year-old Mr Tan Jixiang, an engineering graduate, who will qualify as LPs when the scheme comes into effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We recognise that not all plumbing work needs to be regulated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: PUB has drawn up a list of simple plumbing works which do not affect the integrity of the water supply or sanitary network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For instance, the changing of the flushing mechanism within a flushing cistern and the changing of taps need not be carried out by an LP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Such excluded works will be set out in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Consumers can refer to the PUB website for the list of such works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For works that do require an LP, they will also be able to refer to the website for the online database of LPs when the new scheme takes effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: It is crucial for public health and safety reasons for there to be regulatory oversight over the quality of drinking water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Regulation of water quality is currently the responsibility of the National Environment Agency's (NEA's) Drinking Water Unit (DWU) and PUB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: However, NEA's existing powers do not cover drinking water that is provided free of charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: As the public looks to PUB for any water quality-related matters, PUB remains the primary responder.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: If the failure was the result of any other cause, then the matter will be referred to DWU.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: DWU will also continue to have oversight over the quality of the drinking water provided by PUB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: With these enhancements to our regulatory system, we can be assured that our drinking water will continue to be clean, wholesome and safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Besides these, the Bill includes other amendments to improve operations and allow for the smooth functioning of PUB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The proposed enhancements to the Public Utilities Act are forward-looking and aim to ensure that good and safe water continues to be conveyed and enjoyed by all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We have seen from water crises around the world how things can go from right to wrong very quickly, often with just one misstep in the long complex chain of supplying water.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Once public confidence in their water supply is lost, it is hard to regain, and affected communities take years to recover.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We are determined never to let this happen and will continue to strengthen our water system so that Singaporeans will always have access to good, wholesome water.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Plumbing works have become more integrated and concealed, presenting higher risk of cross-contamination between the water and sanitary systems if not built properly by plumbers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, many of our homes are getting older, they will need repairs and upgrades and these have attracted many smaller contractors, and even freelancers, working on jobs into our homes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am not sure all of them are, indeed, qualified persons under the existing Act.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Our water supply, sanitary and drainage system is an important artery, just like the blood vessels that deliver oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the body tissues.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am pleased to understand that SPS and the Singapore Sanitary Ware Importers and Exporters Association have been in conversation with PUB.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We all know how messy it can be if you have problems with sanitary plumbing works and it is good that PUB is ensuring that these plumbers get the right training.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I believe if we get plumbers who are competently trained in different areas of plumbing, then it would also be good for home owners as they do not have to run around scouting for different plumbers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some unlicensed plumbers, including those from across the Causeway, may be cheap, but they may be doing work through trial and error, or based on whatever experience they have amassed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They may not properly understand the mechanics in plumbing.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, I heard from a home owner who, for several years, have to suffer from water hammer or noises from his water pipes because they were not properly installed before they were concealed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is worse is that there is no way to seek redress as he could not locate or contact the plumber.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Next is the issue of the quality of the material.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many residents told me that many plumbers nowadays come from across the Causeway.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They come in vans and cars or even carry a few pieces on motorbikes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How do we ensure that the materials that they use, such as pipes and fittings, are meeting Singapore's standards?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is PUB working with our Immigration and Checkpoints Authority to address this problem?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Next, is their workmanship up to the standards required by PUB?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is there sufficient capacity to train all existing plumbers?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The last concern is how to ensure that this will not be just another layer of rubber stamping.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Plumbing systems are like the city's arteries.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Government should make sure that the plumbing courses offered on the market are comprehensive and keeping up with the times.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Only by doing so can we ensure the quality of our plumbers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many people these days look for plumbers on the Internet.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many plumbers from neighbouring countries come directly to our homes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How can the Government prevent unlicensed plumbers from operating in Singapore?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Another problem is that plumbing materials can be easily brought in from other countries, even unauthorised models.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Will the authorities pay attention to this problem?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The Public Utilities (Amendment) Bill is a step in the right direction and consumers can expect to benefit from having peace of mind knowing that public health standards are maintained and their interests are better protected.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The importance of a plumbing system in a modern and densely populated city like ours cannot be understated.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: A badly designed or maintained water reticulation or sanitary system is a recipe for disaster.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: A case in point was the contamination of the water supply system in a mixed development in Bukit Timah in August 2000, where over a hundred people were sickened by contaminated water in the incident.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: While legislation and licensing can help raise the competency of the plumbing industry, experience does matter when it comes to giving consumers peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In the water contamination case cited earlier, the plumber appointed by the management corporation was licensed but he could neither anticipate the potential risk of the badly designed water supply system nor prevent the contamination from happening.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some of these seasoned plumbers are non-English speaking and may only converse in their native mother tongues or dialects, but they are armed with a wealth of knowledge and experience honed from the school of hard knocks.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: For some of them, plumbing may be the only tools of the trade they know, and their livelihood would come to an end in two months’ time, if they are unable to qualify for an LP licence.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: While I support the Bill, I wish to seek the indulgence of the Minister to look into making some provisions for these plumbers so that they can carry on working until such time when they decide to call it a day.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some of their work involves only replacing old pipes, nothing complicated and nothing to design.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can PUB offer the prerequisite courses and assessment for the new LP licence in a language other than English?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can the assessment test be administered in dialects?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can PUB make an exception to waive the prerequisite courses and assessment for plumbers who can prove they have the necessary work experience and have been working in the industry long before even some of us in this Chamber were born?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: When the compulsory MediShield Life was introduced, pensioners were worried they would be worse off but it turned out that their entitled medical benefits under their respective pension schemes remain unchanged.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: MediShield Life coverage, although compulsory, does not kick in for some pensioners.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would the Ministry consider making a similar exception to allow this group of old-school plumbers to continue to ply their trade without the compulsory LP licence, after PUB has made the necessary assessment of their competency?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can PUB issue these plumbers with a non-renewable provisional licence of three years, for example, so that these seniors can have ample time to make other plans and wind down their trade over time?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We are witnessing the passing of a generation of tradesmen and craftsmen from an era gone by.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The good old hawker, the Yellow Top taxi driver, the old-school plumber, to name a few, would probably ply their trade one last time in this decade or so.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: No one is more disrupted than these senior tradesmen and craftsmen as we embrace the digital economy.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Could we not give these Pioneer workers a longer runway to adapt, change and to wind down their trade?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: There is a Motion in the Order Paper today calling for this House to recognise our seniors as a gift to our society.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: It calls on the Government to continue to strengthen support for our seniors to age with dignity and to spearhead community efforts to create a society where they can thrive.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It addresses one of the dilemmas for home owners who are in need of the services of a professional plumber.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Bill, while it imposes on the plumbers to be properly trained and updated on their skillsets, needs to address one important area that would greatly help the thousands of households who would be looking for professional licensed plumbers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are a few ways home owners would commonly go about to get a plumber.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The other is to look up the listing via the web, including the PUB website, and the third is to turn to the Town Council or management corporation strata title (MCST) for assistance.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many licensed plumbers would tell you they can do everything.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But by the time they get to your house, you know they are simply trouble-shooting the problem.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Assuming you want a plumber who can handle a water-hammer issue in your home.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Get our plumbers to specialise in areas like tackling water hammer, regulating water pressure, water tank pumps and so on, so that, besides the general training, they can each add value by having a specialisation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is good that licensed plumbers be proficient in both water service and sanitary plumbing works.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It offers added convenience for consumers, who may otherwise have to engage multiple service providers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope PUB can give more information on its website.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Currently, the PUB website gives the following: licence number, name, block unit number, street name, postal code, business telephone and business hours.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But what is helpful is to also indicate their areas of specialisation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Plumbing as a vocation and means to make a living was fairly popular in post-war Singapore such that, by 1956, SPS was founded to represent the interests of this industry.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many self-employed plumbers picked up and refined their plumbing skills through gaining experience on the job.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Today, many of them are senior citizens but continue to be very active in the industry.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Their job serves as their livelihood in their twilight years.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   I note that registration and invitations for the courses are all being done by email.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My concern is that this can be a challenge for this group of elderly plumbers, many of whom may not be Internet-savvy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They may also not be aware of the procedures to get licensed or even the need to be licensed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can I ask if the Ministry has any measures to help those SPS-registered plumbers who are not Internet savvy?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, what about those who are not registered with SPS and what will be done to reach out to them to get the necessary qualifications?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On this note, I would like to ask if the Ministry has a target to have a minimum number of licensed plumbers as a ratio to the number of flats in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Although the licensing scheme for plumbers was announced last April, some of these freelancers may not be aware that only PUB LPs licensed under this revised scheme will be allowed to install, fix and maintain plumbing systems for water service and sanitary works.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those who have yet to undergo or still undergoing the course, would they be allowed to continue with their livelihood in the interim period?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And, if they are unable to complete the course due to learning difficulties, can the duration be extended?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, as some of these plumbers may not be proficient in English, could the courses be conducted in other languages as well?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This course is required by plumbers without acceptable plumbing qualifications and many elderly freelance plumbers will likely fall into this group.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will assistance be available to those who have difficulties affording it?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): I hope that those affected by this upgrade will see this as an opportunity to pick up new skills and formalise their knowledge.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Ultimately, it would help open opportunities and equip them with modern plumbing skills.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Builder Certificate course will be a worthy investment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Given that there are so many new flats, the demand for their services would certainly increase.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Ultimately, consumers, too, will benefit from having a larger pool of professionals who provide quality plumbing services to tap on.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Efforts to streamline regulations and combine both types of plumbers under a single scheme can only lead to enhance professionalism for the plumbing industry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Enhanced professionalism of our plumbers can only lead to a more reliable water system with fewer faults.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After this period, plumbers who have not undergone additional training will not be able to offer their services.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, I would also like to ask what steps PUB had taken to ensure that our nation's plumbers have been well-informed of these changes and what steps will be taken to ensure a smooth transition for this group.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Were stakeholder consultations conducted prior to the Bill and, if so, what were some of the concerns raised and how were they addressed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Other groups which I believe would be affected that the Senior Minister of State had also mentioned include the handymen who want to upgrade themselves and obtain a plumber's licence.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the information has been published on the PUB website.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But as many in this group are older in their years or less educated, they may need additional assistance navigating these changes and I hope that the Senior Minister of State and the Ministry will consider this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, I also understand that LWSPs are required to attend a mandatory refresher course once every three years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will sanitary plumbers, once under the new LP scheme, be also required to take this course?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, from the consumers' point of view and as many Members have raised, let us, say, if I am renovating my house and need a plumber, how would I know if my usual plumber has obtained a new licence?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the new LPs carry around a card?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, let us, say, if I need repairs for the water pipe in my house, how would I know if I am required to engage the services of an LP or if a freelance handyman would suffice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding the above clarification, Sir, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   I support the Public Utilities (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The new licensing framework for plumbers will make Singapore's qualified plumbers more professional, and it is conducive to the improvement of industry standards.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will also help ensure the quality of water and sanitary services provided to Singaporeans and maintain the standard of our public sanitation.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As the plumbing systems are getting more complex, plumbers must be equipped with the necessary knowledge and skills to ensure the standard and safety of our water, and the health of the water users.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, plumbers must understand the relevant regulations, the designs provided by developers and house owners, and know under what circumstances they should apply for permission from PUB.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The new measures will also allow Singaporeans to enjoy more convenience, both in terms of water service and sanitation works.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They only need one plumber to carry out these two types of work.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although PUB allows unlicensed freelance plumbers to continue to do simple works, such as clearing pipes, changing taps or the hose to the taps, installing, changing or dismantling basins, and replacing floor traps or the cover of the drainage, this new regulation will, nevertheless, greatly affect their livelihood.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many plumbers are experienced older workers who speak dialect mostly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The minimum requirement for applying this course is to have a “workplace Literacy and Numeracy Level 4 Certificate”.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Just like my other colleagues have mentioned, can the authorities consider helping this group of plumbers because the written English test is not to their advantage?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there any way that the Government can help improve their English standard?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lastly, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether foreign plumbers who conduct water or sanitary works are also going to be licensed.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Moreover, does PUB have enough inspectors to check on whether works are done by qualified plumbers?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Louis Ng have spoken on helping existing and would-be plumbers to continue to serve in this important trade and facilitating their entry into the new LP scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PUB announced its intention to roll out the new licensing scheme some 10 months ago, in April last year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even prior to the announcement of the scheme, PUB had engaged SPS extensively.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: After the announcement via several media channels – newspaper, radio, television, including in vernacular languages, as well as circulars – weekly public briefing sessions were held for 10 consecutive weeks to share details with interested stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All of PUB’s LWSPs and members of SPS were invited to the sessions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Other plumbers and members of the public also attended the sessions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To facilitate the transition to the new scheme, additional runs of BCA Academy's Builder Certificate course and PUB’s short inhouse conversion course were mounted.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Among them, there are plumbers who are in their 80s and have qualified to become LPs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Additionally, as noted in my speech earlier, another 25 who have the requisite experience but were neither licensed nor registered with SPS, have completed the necessary courses and will be able to become LPs when the Act comes into effect.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Essentially, these are plumbers with the requisite experience but did not have the licence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They will be licensed when the Act comes into effect.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: During the six-month transition period, water service plumbers and those currently or formerly registered as sanitary plumbers with SPS may continue practising their respective trade pending their licence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For those who have not completed their licensing requirements by the end of the six-month transition period from the effective date of the legislation, they can approach PUB which will assist them on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While we encourage and help as many as possible to upgrade their skills and be certified, there continues to be a role for those who do not have the new licence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, they can carry out plumbing works as long as they are working directly under an LP who will manage and sign off on the works.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Second, they can carry out non-critical simple plumbing works for consumers on their own, such as clearing chokes and installing sinks, bathtubs and showers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There will continue to be a market for such work and a full list of unregulated works can be found on PUB’s website.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Png Eng Huat and Mr Louis Ng expressed concern that some plumbers, especially the older ones, may have difficulties getting certified due to language requirements or financial difficulties.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: (In Mandarin):   A minimum working proficiency of English is necessary, so that licensed plumbers can understand the regulatory requirements, read plans and submit forms to PUB.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While the courses are conducted in English, the instructors take a practical approach in helping participants understand the content.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To accommodate plumbers who cannot manage the written assessment of PUB's two- or three-day conversion course, PUB facilitates oral assessments in other languages, such as Mandarin.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PUB has also worked with the BCA Academy to recognise the "Workplace Literacy and Numeracy Level 4" certificate for entry to the Builder Certificate course.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So far, the plumbers who have engaged PUB are willing to take this course.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Take the case of 50-year-old Mr Anthony Cheng Lai Swee.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: He used to work for plumbing companies that carry out plumbing and sanitary work and is now doing freelance sanitary plumbing works.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When the LP scheme was announced last year in April, he was initially concerned that he did not have the minimum proficiency in English to register for the Builder Certificate course.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the end, Mr Cheng decided to register for the “Workplace Literacy and Numeracy Level 4” course and passed the test, which allowed him to register for the Builder Certificate course.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: He has since completed the theory part of the Builder Certificate course and will be taking the practical part in March 2018.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Cheng was glad that SPS and PUB have been assisting and facilitating him to transit to the LP scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: (In English): As for financial assistance, PUB waives the fees of its conversion course for all existing plumbers on their first attempt and, beyond that, on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Most plumbers whom PUB has engaged thus far have no issues with the course fees.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, if any plumbers face difficulties, I encourage them to contact PUB, and we will see how to further assist them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Gan Thiam Poh expressed concerns over unlicensed foreign plumbers operating in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is illegal for foreigners to work in Singapore without a valid work pass.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Foreign plumbers with valid work passes who wish to practise in Singapore will need to be licensed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Plumbing systems have a significant impact on the quality of tap water and on public health.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I urge consumers, when hiring plumbing services, to go to the register of LWSPs on PUB's website, or call PUB's 24-hour Call Centre at 1800-CALL-PUB, to find these plumbers or verify their status.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This register will be expanded to cover all LPs once the new scheme is implemented.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LPs will also be required to carry an authorised licence card from PUB for verification.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also brought up LPs subcontracting works to non-licensed plumbers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More importantly, even as we enhance the regulatory system, PUB will work with SPS to enhance consumer education so that consumers will be aware of the importance of using LPs for critical plumbing works.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Joan Pereira suggested encouraging LPs to develop specialised skills in specific fields of work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While the LP scheme requires plumbers to be proficient in both water and sanitary plumbing works, they are free to elect the field of work that they wish to practise in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Currently, to help consumers make a better choice when engaging a plumber, the register of LWSPs on PUB's website also indicates the types of services that some plumbers are offering.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When the new scheme takes effect, PUB will extend the listing of types of services offered for sanitary plumbing on the register of LPs on PUB's website as well.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked whether the courses offered at ITE are continually reviewed to keep pace with industry needs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The courses offered are in accordance with Singapore's current plumbing standards, and PUB will continue to work with educational institutions like ITE and BCA Academy to ensure their courses keep pace with industry needs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To conclude, the amendments to this Bill are an important step forward to ensure that Singaporeans continue enjoying clean and safe water.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, I call on Members of the House to give their support to this Bill.
